blocks.text: Easter Island: Anakena and Major Archaeological Sites

provenance.rationale: Summarizes the Word Day 5 full-day excursion through archaeological sites ending at Anakena.

blocks.text:
Breakfast, then a full-day excursion to Anakena, visiting archaeological sites that tell the story of Rapa Nui culture, from its origins and golden age to its deepest crises. Drive along the coast to Ahu Akahanga, then to the Rano Raraku volcano, where most of the Moai were carved and where the greatest number of statues still stands today. Box lunch in nature.

Visit Ahu Tongariki, the largest ceremonial platform, with 15 restored statues, then continue to the Poike Peninsula on the north coast and Ahu Te Pito Kura, home to the largest Moai ever erected outside the quarry. End at Anakena Beach, with its warm turquoise water, white sand, palm trees and the Ahu Nau Nau platform, one of the most beautiful landscapes on the island: time for a walk and a swim. Return to Hanga Roa through the centre of the island.

provenance.rationale: Full Word Day 5 itinerary retained with only the leading day marker removed and paragraphs separated.
The beach name comes directly from the Word Day 5 itinerary paragraph.

blocks.text: Easter Island: Orongo and Rano Kau

provenance.rationale: Headline composed from the Orongo and Rano Kau sites named in the Word Day 6 passage.

blocks.text:
Breakfast, then a morning visit to the ceremonial centre of Orongo. Climb the slopes of the Rano Kau volcano to a viewpoint on the edge of the crater, which holds a beautiful lake with its characteristic vegetation. Then visit the ceremonial village of Orongo, where the island’s leader was chosen each year through a perilous competition: every spring the clans gathered in its stone houses, awaiting the arrival of the sacred Manutara bird to choose the Tangata Manu, the Birdman.

Duration: approximately 4 hours. Meals: breakfast.
